खग: Khaga m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 10, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
खड्गसाधन: Khaḍgasādhana nt.: Name (?) of a chapter (12. 160) in the Śāntiparvan in which the acquisition of the sword is narra-ted 12. 160. 87; also described as ‘acquain-ting (the hearer) with the creation of the sword’ (?) (इत्य् एष प्रथमः कल्पो व्या-ख्यातस् ते सुविस्तरः । असेर् उत्पत्तिसंसर्-गः) 12. 160. 86. Described as best (उत्तम) 12. 160. 87; the origin of the sword was narrated by Bhīṣma, lying on the bed of arrows, to Nakula, who was expert in wielding a sword, at the latter's request 12. 160. 1, 8, 9; a ‘being’ (भूतम्) called ‘sword’ (असि) was conceived by Pitāmaha (मयैतच् चिन्तितं भूतम् असिर् नाम) for the protection of the world and destruction of the enemies of gods; the ‘being’ then gave up its form and became निस्त्रिंश (ततस् तद् रूपम् उत्षृज्य बभौ निस्त्रिंश एव सः) 12. 160. 42-43; the असि or निस्त्रिंश is described as spot-less (विमल) 12. 160. 43, shining (दीप्त) 12. 160. 44; sharp-edged (तीक्ष्णधार) 12. 160. 43; strong (वीर्यवन्त्) 12. 160. 42; warding off अधर्म (अधर्मप्रतिवारण) 12. 160. 44; great (परम) 12. 160. 79; ready to strike like a Kālāntaka (कालान्तक इवोद्यतः) 12. 160. 43; foremost among weapons (अग्र्यः प्रहरणानां च) 12. 160. 83; protector of धर्म (धर्मस्य गोप्तारम्) 12. 160. 64; the interior of which was धर्म (धर्मगर्भ) 12. 160. 67; the असि, after its creation, was given by god Brahman first to Rudra 12. 160. 42, 44; with that निस्त्रिंश in hand Rudra cut off, broke, wounded, tore asunder, split open, and destroyed the Daityas (छिन्दन् भिन्दन् रुजन् कृन्तन् दारयन् प्रमथन्न् अपि । अचरद् दैत्यसंघेषु रुद्रः) 12. 160. 55; god Rudra then honoured Viṣṇu and handed over the sword to him; from Viṣṇu it passed successively through various hands to different persons until from the guardians of the world (लोकपालस्) it came to Manu, the son of Sūrya and lord of men; Manu was asked to protect his subjects with the sword 12. 160. 64-67; from Manu it again changed hands through successive generations of kings until it came from Bharadvāja to Droṇa, then to Kṛpa, and finally from him to Nakula and his brothers (ततस् त्वं भ्रातृभिः सार्धं परमासिम् अवाप्तवान्) 12. 160. 71-79; the असि is governed by the नक्षत्र Kṛttikā, its deity is Agni, its गोत्र is Rohiṇis, and its गुरु is Rudra 12. 160. 80; असि has eight secret names (नामानि रहस्यानि) which were told by Bhīṣma to Nakula: असि, विशसन, खड्ग, तीक्ष्णवर्त्मन्, दुरासद, श्रीगर्भ, विजय, and धर्मपाल 12. 160. 81-82; one who recites the eight secret names of असि gets victory 12. 160. 81; असि should always be worshipped by those who are expert in fight-ing 12. 160. 85; one who listens to this खड्गसाधन obtains fame (in this life) and eternal happiness (in the next world) (लभते पुरुषः कीर्तिं प्रेत्य चानन्त्यम् अश्नुते) 12. 160. 87.
खाण्डवदाह: Khāṇḍavadāha m.: Name of the 19th पर्वन् (खाण्डवदाहाख्यम्) in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 39, 33, 70. It is mentioned (खाण्डवस्य च दाहनम्) in the list of the contents of the Ādiparvan 1. 2. 93; it also narrates the release of Maya from fire and the escape of the snake 1. 2. 94; the incident is referred to by Dhṛta-rāṣṭra in his summary made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 104 and by Vaiśaṃpāyana in his summary made for Janamejaya 1. 55. 35-38; these incidents form the contents of the अध्यायस् 1. 214-225.
खाण्डव: Khāṇḍava m., nt.: Name of a forest. A. Location: Situated in the Kurukṣetra (यस्य (i. e. तक्षकस्य) वासः कुरु-क्षेत्रे खाण्डवे चाभवत् सदा) 1. 3. 144; near the river Yamunā 1. 214. 14; 1. 215. 1. B. Description: Called दाव 1. 215. 6-7, 9-10, 12; 1. 216. 31, 34; 1. 218. 19 (?); 1. 219. 3 (?), 10, 22; 1. 220. 31; 1. 223. 22; 1. 225. 15; 4. 2. 9; 4. 34. 14; वन 1. 216. 33; 1. 217. 22; 1. 218. 2, 4; 1. 220. 1, 17, 20; 1. 224. 7; 1. 225. 5; महावन 1. 215. 18; प्रस्थ 8. 29. 18; it had sanctuaries (?) for manes and gods (which could not offer shelter to animals when the forest was on fire) (न चालभन्त ते शर्म … पितृ-देवनिवासेषु) 1. 219. 27. C. Inhabitants: Demons (दानवाः), Rākṣasas, Nāgas, and animals like hyenas (तरक्षु), bears, ele-phants, tigers, lions, deer, buffalos and birds— all lived in the Khāṇḍava (खाण्डवालोयाः) 1. 219. 1, 2; Takṣaka, friend of Indra, to-gether with his followers (सगणः) and his son Aśvasena lived there 1. 3. 144, 145; 1. 215. 7. D. Agni's desire to burn the forest: Agni approached Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna to seek their help in fulfilling his desire to burn the Khāṇḍava; since Indra's friend Takṣaka lived in the forest, he foiled all Agni's ear-lier attempts to burn it 1. 215. 1-12; 1. 223. 25; 3. 46. 40; 4. 34. 14; E. Arjuna's request for weapons: Hearing Agni's request Arjuna asked for suitable weapons for him-self and Kṛṣṇa so that both of them could foil Indra's attempt to pour water on the great forest 1. 215. 13-18; this was arranged by Agni 1. 216. 1-27. F. Burning of the forest: The burning described 1. 216. 33-34; 1. 217-219; 1. 220. 32; the burning was so frightful that it appeared as if the end of Aeon had set in (ददाह खाण्डवं क्रुद्धो युगान्तम् इव दर्शयन्) 1. 216. 32. G. Duration: The forest was burning for six days (पावकश् चापि तं दावं दग्ध्वा समृगपक्सिणम् । अहानि पञ्च चैकं च विरराम सुतर्पितः) 1. 225. 15. H. Who were saved from the fire: (i) The Pannaga Takṣaka, since he was not present at the Khāṇḍava at the time of the burning 1. 218. 4; 1. 219. 13; (ii) His son Aśvasena was present in the Khāṇḍava but was saved by his mother, who swallowed him, and by Indra who released gusts of wind 1. 218. 4-9; (iii) Asura Maya who sought shelter with Arjuna when Kṛṣṇa wanted to kill him 1. 219. 35-39; (iv) Four young sons (Śārṅga birds) of Mandapāla were saved by Agni at their father's request (प्रदहन् खाण्डवं दावं मम पुत्रान् विसर्जय) 1. 220. 31-32; 20-21; 1. 223. 22; they were left behind in the Khāṇḍava by their mother as they did not listen to her advice to enter a mouse hole to save themselves 1. 222. 16; actually, at the time of the conflagration, only six were not burnt by Agni, viz. Aśvasena, Maya, and four Śārṅgaka birds 1. 219. 40; 1. 220. 2, 4. I. Why was the forest burnt: Destruction of the Khāṇḍava was ordained — this was told to Indra by an invisible voice (वाग् उवाचा-शरीरिणी … दिष्टं चानुपश्यैतत् खाण्डव-स्य विनाशनम्) 1. 219. 12, 18; when Arjuna was born an invisible voice had foretold that Agni would burn the forest with the help of Arjuna 1. 114. 28, 32; 8. 48. 7; but Agni is said to have burnt the forest to make the world free from fear (भगवान् अपि तिग्मांशुः समिद्धं खाण्डवं वनम् । ददाह सह कृष्णाभ्यां जनयञ् जगतो ऽभयम्) 1. 225. 5. J. Allusions in the Ādi and the other पर्वन्स् to the Khāṇḍavadāha: (i) Agni desirous of burning the Khāṇḍava appro-ached Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa 4. 2. 9; (ii) Agni arranged to get two inexhaustible quivers and the Gāṇḍīva bow for Arjuna and the Cakra for Kṛṣṇa 1. 2. 93; 3. 40. 36; 3. 157. 20; 5. 155. 7; 7. 10. 21; 17. 1. 37-39; (iii) Agni burnt the Khāṇḍava forest with the help of Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa and was satiated 1. 1. 104; 1. 55. 35; 3. 46. 14; 4. 18. 10; 4. 35. 10; 5. 51. 9; 5. 59. 8; 5. 61. 8; 6. 94. 5; 7. 10. 21; 8. 65. 15; 8. 66. 23; 13. 143. 23; 15. 46. 11; 17. 1. 36; (iv) Arjuna (and Kṛṣṇa) fighting a war with Indra and other gods and defeating them at the Khāṇḍava forest: 1. 1. 104; 3. 157. 20; 5. 22. 13; 5. 51. 9; 5. 155. 26; 6. 94. 5; 7. 160. 15; 8. 29. 18; 8. 31. 9; 13. 143. 23; (v) Aśvasena's escape from the Khāṇḍava fire: 8. 66. 23. K. Similes: (1) Bhīma wanted to release his wrath on Duryodhana as Arjuna released fire on the Khāṇḍava (खाण्डवे ऽग्निम् इवार्जुनः) 9. 32. 30; (2) Bhīma wanted to release his wrath on Duryo-dhana as Fire released (his wrath) on the Khāṇḍava (खाण्डवे पावको यथा) 9. 55. 16; (3) When the forest (Khāṇḍava, not directly named) was on fire it looked like the golden Meru mountain which is of great lustre (दह्यतस् तस्य विबभौ रूपं दावस्य भारत । मेरोर् इव नगेन्द्रस्य काञ्चनस्य महाद्युतेः ॥ ) 1. 216. 34.
खश: Khaśa m. (pl.): Name of a people (identical with Khaśikas ?) A. Location: They lived between mountains Meru and Mandara under the pleasant shade of bamboos and reeds along the river Śailodā 2. 48. 2-3 (for citations see Ekāśanājyoha). B. Description: Describ-ed as goat-faced (बस्तमुख) 7. 97. 39; fierce and cruel (उग्राश् च क्रूरकर्मा-णः) 8. 51. 18; wrathful, fond of battles, strong and of firm fists (?) (संरम्भिणो युद्धशौण्डा बलिनो दृब्धपाणयः) 8. 51. 19; they could not be conquered by any one except by Arjuna (न शक्या युधिनिर्-जेतुं त्वदन्येन परंतप) 8. 51. 20. C. Weapons: They fought with axes, spears and stones (अयोहस्त, शूलहस्त, अश्म-वृष्टिं समन्ततः … क्सिप्तां क्सिप्तां) 7. 97. 39; also with शक्तिस्, प्रासस्, and quivers (i. e. arrows stored in तूणीरस्) 8. 15. 9. D. Epic events: (1) Kings of Khaśas brought as tribute for the Rājasūya heaps of पिपीलिक gold, to be measured by द्रोणस् (ते वै पिपीलिकं नाम … जात-रूपं द्रोणमेयम् अहार्षुः) 2. 48. 3-4; (2) Ulūka mentioned Khaśas among those who had joined the army of Duryo-dhana (राजचमूं समेताम्) 5. 158. 19-20; (3) On the fourteenth day of war, Sātyaki repulsed with नाराच arrows stones showered on him again and again by Khaśas 7. 97. 39; (4) On the sixteenth day, Pāṇḍya killed Khaśas and others fighting on horse-backs, along with their horses (अश्वारोहान् हयान् अपि) 8. 15. 9 [see Khaśika].
खशिक: Khaśika m. (pl.): Name of a people (identical with Khaśas ?) Mentioned by Saṃjaya among the northern Mlecchas of Bhāratavarṣa (उत्त-राश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … खशिकाश् च तुखाराश् च) 6. 10. 63, 66, 5 [See Khaśa].
